main_body: A hexagonal coffin lid with a cross, drawn almost entirely as a flat lid seen from above and tapering toward the foot; no separate south face below it.
top_band: The whole body is a single lid surface in orange-brown tones from row 2 to row 30. There is no distinct lighter top band followed by a front edge step.
evidence: The coffin is a plan view of its lid: a tapered hexagonal slab with a cross inlay and a dark outline all round. Its bottom is a thin dark edge at rows 29-30, with only a darker block at the lower right hinting at depth. No front face reads as a vertical surface below the lid, which matches the 'top-down slab (no front)' failure in the guide.

style.evidence: The outline is dark brown, tinted to match the wood. The lid has about 3-4 steps of brown, with a small amount of vertical grain, and the cross is a flat yellow with a darker band. The lid contains large areas of flat colour with little grain or speckle. It is cleaner and thinner than the stall and well references, which carry more tones and texture per tile.
